text:
Situation: Heparin sodium has been on FDA's drug shortage list since 2017-11-14 and remains current as of 2026-10-21. The listing includes B. Braun Medical Inc., Baxter Healthcare, Fresenius Kabi USA LLC, and Hospira Inc. as affected companies. Current inventory across Corvale sites ranges from 5.9 to 31.7 days of supply depending on formulation and location.

Why (FDA record): FDA first posted the heparin sodium shortage on 2017-11-14. Hospira's plant (FEI 1925262) was inspected on 2017-10-27 and classified VAI, 18 days before the shortage posting. Baxter's plant (FEI 1025114) was inspected on 2016-02-26 and classified OAI, 627 days before the posting. Baxter's plant (FEI 2618677) received a Warning Letter on 2017-02-14, 273 days before the posting.

Our position: The rule-based best option is to buy from BE Pharmaceuticals Inc., which is not on FDA's shortage list today. Four additional suppliers (Civica, Inc., Gland Pharma Limited, Hepalink USA Inc., Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA Inc.) also do not appear on the current shortage list. None of these suppliers' labels name plants we could verify.

Recommended actions:
1. Buyer to initiate purchase from BE Pharmaceuticals Inc. — requires P&T committee approval.
2. Buyer to evaluate Civica, Inc., Gland Pharma Limited, Hepalink USA Inc., and Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA Inc. as secondary sources — requires P&T committee approval for each.
3. Buyer to monitor FDA shortage list weekly for status changes — requires pharmacy director approval.

Not recommended: Switching to alternative anticoagulants or changing heparin protocols; clinical decisions remain with treating clinicians and the committee.
